question: Does the design hold — selected approach, spike-backed risk evidence, expected surface and semantics, and proof per AC — ready to baseline implementation?

artifacts.summary: Ideation complete (worker 5f557e70, report in entity, commit a504e7bd). Design: single-owner bootstrap — frontdoor keeps argv-only duties; extension gate PI_SPACEDOCK_LAUNCH=1 (not SPACEDOCK_BIN, rejected alternative recorded); two safety nets (ready-gate refusal at launch, contract-level version abort). Spike ran first and changed the design twice: /skill:first-officer expands only on user input, so bootstrap wording points at the <available_skills> listing; duplicate registration is real on this machine (dev-link shadows installed git package), making the flag + self-check load-bearing. Method finding recorded: AC proofs specified as deterministic artifacts, never model self-report. Surface +230 net (+281/−52) across 6 files, tolerance ±60 net / ±2 files; five observable semantics declared; four concrete doc diffs; AC-1..AC-8 with proof owner + falsifying edit each.
